decisive_spans.text: MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5

response.rationale: Spondylodiscitis is supported by MRI findings of both disc and vertebral body involvement, as well as clinical symptoms and positive blood cultures. Osteomyelitis is also supported by MRI findings and clinical presentation, but spondylodiscitis is a more specific diagnosis given the involvement of both the disc and adjacent vertebrae. Discitis is supported by MRI findings consistent with disc infection, but spondylodiscitis is a more comprehensive diagnosis. Enterobacter cloacae infection is a causative agent, not the diagnosis of the spinal condition. Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is a past medical history and not the current diagnosis.
